newsitem.title: CANADA: Moderator collapses in Canada election debate.
newsitem.headline: Moderator collapses in Canada election debate.

text.p: Canada's French-language televised debate for the June 2 federal election came to an abrupt halt on Tuesday when the moderator collapsed just as leaders were about to debate the crucial issue of Quebec independence.

Moderator Claire Lamarche fell ill and spectators were asked to leave the hall just as the five political party leaders were about to attack the issue of national unity. Lamarche was taken out on a stretcher.
The debate was about two hours into its scheduled 2-1/2 hours. The party leaders decided to conclude the debate for the evening and for the rest of the campaign.

Information about Lamarche's condition was not immediately available, but people in the room said the hall was stuffy. As she was carried out of the auditorium wrapped in blankets, Lamarche was conscious and moaning about the warmth in the auditorium.
The collapse came as the debate reached a peak of tension. Prime Minister Jean Chretien was asked if he would recognize a vote in favor of Quebec sovereignty if it were by a slim margin.
In 1995, people in French-speaking Quebec voted 50.6 percent against Quebec separation, while 49.4 percent voted in favor of separation, prompting federalist forces to claim victory.
